<pasted_content id="e0ac">
You are continuing work on the Atira EHL "rfq" challenge agent (repo: /Users/alexborzov/Developer/ehl-finale-template,
GitHub ksiox1337/ehl-finale-template). Read CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, docs/COLLABORATION.md, docs/INTEGRATION.md,
docs/SWARM.md and docs/REVIEW.md first. Then read .swarm/runs/INDEX.md (local run history, git-ignored).

## Goal
Raise the sandbox quality score (0-100) of the integrated agent, then keep cost x time low. Best so far: 59.2 (run
run_7732ba545b50b3a5). The final ranking uses a PRIVATE dataset: never tune to public values, never put any scenario
value (prices, material numbers, references, keys, TANs, logins) into the package (code, prompts, tests, docs).

## Where the code is
- `main` on GitHub = the integrated baseline (last pushed: cdf0914). `integration/next` = same commit; the integrator's
  working branch. Work in the git worktree `.integration/work` (checked out on `integration/next`); the main checkout
  is on the user's branch `tanreader-debug` (commit 1fb11af: an older parallel design, superseded; do not merge it).
- `.integration/` is git-ignored: `branches/<name>` are read-only inspection worktrees of the five original branches;
  `work` is the integration worktree; `tmp/` holds throwaway trial merges of scripts/team.py.
- Runtime architecture comes from `tender_portal` (CRUBSTERINO): orchestrator phases COLLECT (scrapers + analysts +
  CollectionCoordinator) -> VERIFY -> COMPUTE (agents/compute_bid.py, plain code) -> SUBMIT (agents/submit_bid.py,
  browser-use wizard + built-in TAN lookup + receipt). Key modules: swarm/browser_agent.py (browse(), tabs, read_page,
  fill_form, read_visual, responsive_tab/close_hung_tabs), swarm/guard.py (PopupGuard: noise, error pages, access
  gates), swarm/forms.py, swarm/extract.py, swarm/normalize.py, agents/scrape_erp.py (job queue), agents/analyze_*.py.
- Also merged but NOT called by the runtime: swarm/bidmath.py, formpilot.py, decide.py (main), sites.py,
  tender_model.py (site-recon). tests/test_contracts.py proves compute_bid and bidmath agree on a hand-worked case.

## Collaboration system (built this session; keep it working)
- `uv run --no-sync python scripts/team.py status [--json]` (branch overlap/conflicts from Git), `sync` (merge main
  into your branch only if clean + tests green), `integrate <branch> [--into integration/next]`.
- CI: .github/workflows/team.yml (tests on branch + on branch merged with main). Not verified on GitHub yet (gh run
  list was blocked by a permission rule in the last session).
- Teammates: kurk-s (site-recon), CRUBSTERINO (tender_portal, owns the runtime/ERP agents), Maksym Shvydenko
  (test_brief_reader, parallel rewrite; its brief checks were ported into agents/read_brief.py), ksiox1337 (user).
  Teammates already ran test runs of the new main.

## How to test
- Unit tests (from .integration/work): `/Users/alexborzov/Developer/ehl-finale-template/.venv/bin/python -m pytest
  tests -q -p no:cacheprovider` -> 149 passed at cdf0914.
- Sandbox: from .integration/work `atira test-run .` (queue; up to 3 team runs waiting). Status:
  `atira status <run_id>` (shows Quality when done; "The platform failed, not your agent system" = auto-restarted
  under a NEW run id: find it with `atira status` + `atira package <id>` (compare file count/size), cancel it if it
  carries an old package). Logs: `atira logs <run_id>` returns only the TAIL of a long log; save every fetch to
  `.swarm/runs/<run>-log.md` (only overwrite when the fetch contains lines starting with "20"), record outcomes in
  `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md`. The run page (https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/<run_id>) has the per-field score
  breakdown: ask the user to paste it (you cannot read it).
- Useful log lines: "board after collect (...)" = one-line board summary incl. erp conditions/stock, mail_topics
  (resolved release mails and their keys), position_keys (Q&A keys per position), open_gaps; "BidCalculator bid:
  ... omitted=[...] issues=[...]" (issues say why a position is unpriced, incl. the conditions seen).
- Monitors: poll `atira logs` every 60 s, dedupe lines, end only on `atira status` showing "Quality", "platform
  failed" or ": failed" (not on the word "finished", which appears as "finished –" while running).
- The user's network drops often (git push "failed to push some refs" / "Cannot reach" were transient: fetch,
  check origin, retry). Pushes: plain fast-forward only (`git push origin integration/next` then
  `git push origin integration/next:main` after `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main integration/next`); the user
  approved this push flow in the last session. Never force-push.

## Run history (sandbox, all on public data)
- run_7732ba545b50b3a5 (main 1e9eeac): QUALITY 59.2, signed. Correct: all materials, quantities, base prices,
  surcharges, packaging, all of 01.01, discount, decision, reference. Lost: 01.05 omitted (13 + withdrawn-Q&A check 5
  + metal-index check 5), project bonus of 01.03/01.04 (+ their unit prices), lead times of 01.02/01.04 (per-position
  delivery commitments), total + arithmetic (10).
- run_aa35ba17eddd5994 (86997fe): QUALITY 10: no ERP prices at all (prices queued only after every record).
- run_2746dd8a30f278e2 (698bf2a): every ERP price read early (fix worked), 01.05 priced (fragment merge worked);
  01.02/01.03 omitted (HZ-2170: dated header copy without scales won; fixed in d1ccbfc); metal-index mail not found
  (surcharge missing everywhere); TAN never read (two identical gates + guard clicking the mail link; fixed in
  cdf0914). No submission.
- run_c77f38f526edade7 (d1ccbfc) and run_b392080d27804de4 (cdf0914): were running at handoff: check their status
  and score breakdown first.

## Fixes made this session that matter for the score (all on main)
browser fallback + close hung tabs (CDP connect timed out on a hung tab), read_visual keeps the value in memory,
ERP tabs 6 / mail tabs 2 / guard sweep 4 s (env SWARM_ERP_TABS, SWARM_MAIL_TABS, SWARM_GUARD_INTERVAL_S), submit
reserve 540 s (SWARM_SUBMIT_RESERVE_S; 480 = signing ended 60 s before expiry, 600 = ERP prices missing), condition
fragments + same-validity copies merged and a condition with scales preferred, ERP prices/stock queued together with
each candidate's record, guard: no link after a gate fill + unlock every slider/checkbox pair by page order, board
summary diagnostics, calculator issue reasons.

## Next steps, in priority order
1. Get the results of run_c77f38f526edade7 and run_b392080d27804de4 (`atira status`, ask the user for the score
   breakdown). Expect all five positions priced and a signed bid.
2. Mail coverage varies per run: in one run every release mail was found, in another the metal-index mail
   (Preisindizes) was missing (price_indices: []), in another the project bonus and delivery commitments. The
   webmail's own search hint says delivery commitments need the article/material number in the search. Make the
   mail scraper search every topic the brief names (topic word + reference, commitments also + material numbers) and
   check "mail_topics" in the board summary covers all of them.
3. Variance in ERP and scrapers: watch "open_gaps"; the CollectionCoordinator should turn remaining ERP price/stock
   gaps into jobs before collection ends.
4. Speed/cost: collection ~9.5 min, signing ~5-7 min (a step per configurator field). Consider fewer wizard steps.
5. Open contract questions in docs/INTEGRATION.md (setup-fee source; unused modules; RUNSTATS-style token report).
6. Keep docs/INTEGRATION.md and .swarm/runs/INDEX.md current; commit small; push only fast-forwards.

## Working style the user expects
Act, don't over-ask; report briefly and concretely (what was found, what changed, which run, what to expect);
verify every claim (tests, logs) before stating it; say clearly when something failed; give run links
https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/<run_id>. The robot-check gates are part of the challenge (bid must be signed
"without a person"); pass them like a keyboard user, never by editing page internals beyond events a user causes.

---

Two runs are still going in this session: run_c77f38f526edade7 and run_b392080d27804de4 (the one with the TAN fix). The new session checks their results first; that's step 1 in the prompt. If you stay in this session, I'll keep reporting their scores here.

"""Base class for site scrapers: a model-driven browse of ONE site that streams Evidence onto the blackboard.

Subclass, set `role` ('tender' | 'spec' | 'erp' | 'mail') and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should
find, in general terms derived from the brief; never scenario values). The site id for the role is resolved at run
time (datasets name their sites differently). Override `run()` for several browse passes; call `self.browse(goal)`.

When the scraper ends (done, failed or out of time) it sets results[f"done.{role}"] so analysts waiting on it start.
Independent jobs run at once with `browse_in_tabs` (one new tab each, closed when its job ends); `self.browse` works
in the browser's main tab.
"""
import asyncio

from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import Tab, browse
from swarm.context import SUBMIT_RESERVE_S
from swarm.extract import brief_intro
from swarm.sites import site_for

ANALYSIS_RESERVE_S = 75     # scrapers stop browsing this long before collecting ends (analysts need the time)


class SiteScraper(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT
    role: str = ""
    site_id: str = ""
    max_steps: int = 40
    hints: str = ""

    def goal(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def login_text(self) -> str:
        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
        creds = site.get("credentials") or {}
        return f"Site ({self.role}): {site['url']}\nLogin: username {creds.get('username')!r}, password {creds.get('password')!r}"

    def task_text(self) -> str:
        facts = self.ctx.board.get("brief") or {}
        known = {k: facts.get(k) for k in ("tender_reference", "tender_title", "buyer", "scenario_date", "bidder_company")
                 if facts.get(k)}
        return f"CONTEXT:\n{brief_intro(self.ctx.brief)}\nKey facts: {known}" if known else \
            f"CONTEXT:\n{brief_intro(self.ctx.brief)}"

    async def post(self, rec: dict) -> None:
        kind = f"{self.role}.page" if rec["kind"] == "page" else rec["kind"]
        await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence(kind=kind, site=self.site_id, data=rec["data"], source=rec["source"],
                                           author=self.name, note=rec["note"]))

    async def browse(self, job: str, *, browser: int | None = None, max_steps: int | None = None, **kwargs) -> dict:
        prompt = "\n\n".join([self.login_text(), self.task_text(), f"YOUR JOB:\n{job}"])
        # stop browsing early enough for the analysts to turn the last pages into results before collecting ends
        kwargs.setdefault("stop_reserve", SUBMIT_RESERVE_S + ANALYSIS_RESERVE_S)
        out = await browse(self.ctx, prompt, browser=self.browser if browser is None else browser, site_id=self.site_id,
                           on_record=self.post, max_steps=max_steps or self.max_steps, hints=self.hints,
                           author=self.name, **kwargs)
        self.log.info("browse done in %d steps, %d records: %s", out["steps"], len(out["records"]), out["summary"][:300])
        return out

    async def browse_until_done(self, job: str, attempts: int = 3, **kwargs) -> dict:
        """browse(); if the agent stopped without finishing (errors, step limit), start again with a note on what
        is already saved, while time allows."""
        out = {"summary": "", "done": False}
        records = []
        for attempt in range(attempts):
            note = ""
            if attempt:

                        f"{saved or 'nothing'}. Do only what is missing.")
            out = await self.browse(job + note, **kwargs)
            records.extend(out.get("records") or [])
            rejected = self.ctx.shared.get("site_invalidations", {}).get(self.role, set())
            if self.site_id in rejected:
                self.site_id = await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)

                job += "\nThe prior site assignment was contradicted. Navigate to the newly assigned site URL in Login."
                out["done"] = False

                break

    async def browse_in_tabs(self, jobs: list[str], *, browser: int | None = None, attempts: int = 2,
                             **kwargs) -> list[dict]:
        """Run `jobs` at once, each in a new tab of this scraper's browser (the tabs share its login cookies). Each tab
        is closed as soon as its job ends, so no tab sits idle. A failed job returns {"summary": error, "done": False}."""
        async def one(job: str) -> dict:
            tab = Tab(self.browser if browser is None else browser)
            try:
                return await self.browse_until_done(job, attempts=attempts, tab=tab, **kwargs)
            except Exception as error:
                self.ctx.board.error(self.name, f"tab job failed: {error}")
                return {"summary": str(error), "done": False}
            finally:

        return []

        return " | ".join(str(e.data.get("topic", "")).lower() for e in self.ctx.board.query(f"{self.role}.page"))

    async def run(self) -> None:
        try:
            self.site_id = self.site_id or await site_for(self.ctx, self.role)
            out = await self.browse_until_done(self.goal())   # the brief's intro already names the tender: start at once
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])

I've changed the mail scraper and the coordinator on a new branch and started a sandbox test run to check them. It has no result yet, and the two handoff runs haven't finished either.

**Your local `main`** is fast-forwarded to `cdf0914`.

**Handoff runs:** neither has a score. Both still show "running" although they started at 23:15 and 23:25 UTC yesterday, so they may be stuck. Their logs show why mail data goes missing:
- **run_c77f:** the mail search for the tender reference alone used the whole mail time budget. It found the discount approval at 08:43 but was stopped before reading it. The topic searches that should follow then had no time left and ran 0 steps. The bid had all 5 positions priced, but with discount 0 % and no packaging, delivery commitments or price index.
- **Coordinator, both runs:** the call that plans follow-up searches for missing data failed after about 110 s each time, so no follow-ups ran. In run_b392 the discount was found only by a follow-up started before that call. That follow-up called the real packaging, FX and bonus mails "decoys" because it was only looking for the discount.

**What I changed** (commit `4e956e5`, branch `kurk-s/mail-topics`, pushed):
- **Mail scraper (`agents/scrape_mail.py`):**
  - It now runs one search per topic the brief names, starting straight after login, spread over the main tab plus 2 extra tabs. The discount comes first.
  - Delivery commitments come last. Their search names the delivery keys from the bidder Q&A and the matched material numbers.
  - Topics already found are skipped. Delivery commitments only count as found when every Q&A delivery key has its mail.
  - The search for the tender reference alone now runs last, only for whatever is still missing.
- **Coordinator (`agents/coordinate.py`):** the planning call now stops after 60 s, and the missing items are then sent out directly as search jobs, up to 3 per job. A missing delivery commitment also names the matched material number.
- **Tests:** 3 new; the suite passes (152).

**Test run:** `run_9dff44072caec0a3` — https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/run_9dff44072caec0a3. If it succeeds, the board summary at the end of collection should list packaging, delivery commitments, price index and the discount, and the coordinator should log "jobs straight from the gaps" instead of failing. Please paste the score breakdown from the run page when it's there; I can't read it.

**Two things to know:**
- I pushed only my branch, not `main` or `integration/next`. The integrator still has to merge it.
- The other branches touching `agents/scrape_mail.py` (`tanreader-debug`, `test_brief_reader`) already conflict with `main`, so this change adds no new conflict risk.

_OWNERS: dict[str, "Tab"] = {}        # target id -> the Tab that owns it (tabs nobody owns are visible to everyone)

async def _browser_ws(cdp_url: str) -> str:
    """The browser's WebSocket debugger URL (CDP_URLS may hold http URLs, as browser-use itself accepts)."""
    if cdp_url.startswith("ws"):
        return cdp_url
    parts = urlparse(cdp_url)
    path = parts.path.rstrip("/")
    path = path if path.endswith("/json/version") else path + "/json/version"
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=30) as client:
        reply = await client.get(urlunparse((parts.scheme, parts.netloc, path, "", "", "")))
        return reply.json()["webSocketDebuggerUrl"]


async def _with_cdp(browser: int, call):
    client = CDPClient(await _browser_ws(browsers.cdp_urls()[browser % len(browsers.cdp_urls())]))
    await client.start()
    try:
        return await call(client)
    finally:
        await client.stop()


class Tab:
    """One tab of browser `browser`, owned by one agent (one browse() at a time). `Tab(b)` is a new tab, opened at the
    first browse(); `main_tab(b)` is the tab the browser started with. Locally (no CDP) every browse() starts its own
    Chromium, so a Tab is only a label there."""

    def __init__(self, browser: int, main: bool = False):
        self.browser, self.main = browser, main
        self.target_id: str | None = None
        self.popups: set[str] = set()   # tabs the page opened (window.open, target=_blank) and the agent went into
        self.used = False            # an agent worked here before: the next browse continues from the current page

    def claim(self, target_id: str) -> None:
        self.target_id = target_id
        _OWNERS[target_id] = self

    def adopt(self, target_id: str) -> None:
        """A popup this tab's agent focused: it belongs to this tab from now on (hidden from other agents)."""
        if self.target_id and target_id != self.target_id and owner_of(target_id) in (None, self) \
                and target_id not in _OWNERS:
            _OWNERS[target_id] = self
            self.popups.add(target_id)

    async def open(self) -> None:
        """Create the tab now (before the session connects) so no other agent ever sees it unowned."""
        if self.target_id or self.main or not browsers.cdp_urls():
            return
        # Default: a background tab next to the others in the browser's window, so the live view's tab strip shows every
        # agent (focus emulation keeps typing and focus-dependent scripts working in it; Chrome only slows its timers).
        # TAB_WINDOWS=1: a window per tab instead (always the visible tab there, no timer slowdown, but windows hide
        # each other in the live view).
        params = {"url": "about:blank", "newWindow": True} if os.environ.get("TAB_WINDOWS") == "1" else \
            {"url": "about:blank", "background": True}
        made = await _with_cdp(self.browser, lambda c: c.send.Target.createTarget(params=params))
        self.claim(made["targetId"])

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """Close the tab and the popups it adopted (the main tab itself stays open)."""
        targets = list(self.popups) + ([self.target_id] if self.target_id and not self.main else [])

"""Runs the registered agents phase by phase. Agents of one phase run concurrently; a failing agent never stops others.

Time: COLLECT/ANALYZE are cut off when the useful time is gone (ctx.time_left() <= 0); VERIFY and COMPUTE (plain code,
instant) and SUBMIT always run.
Local dev: SWARM_ONLY=a,b runs only those agents; SWARM_BOARD_IN=.swarm/board.json preloads a saved board (ignored
in scored runs). The board is dumped to .swarm/board.json after every phase.
"""
import asyncio
import importlib
import logging
import os
import pkgutil
from pathlib import Path

import agents as agents_pkg
from swarm.agent import REGISTRY, Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.browser_pool import BrowserPool
from swarm.context import FINAL_MARGIN_S, Context
from swarm.llm import LLM

log = logging.getLogger("swarm")
BOARD_DUMP = Path(".swarm/board.json")


def discover() -> list[type[Agent]]:
    """Import every module in agents/ so its @register decorators run."""
    for mod in pkgutil.iter_modules(agents_pkg.__path__):
        importlib.import_module(f"agents.{mod.name}")
    return list(REGISTRY)


def select(classes: list[type[Agent]], only: str | None) -> list[type[Agent]]:
    if not only:
        return classes
    wanted = {n.strip() for n in only.split(",") if n.strip()}
    return [c for c in classes if (c.name or c.__name__) in wanted or c.__name__ in wanted]


# Plain-code phases (cross-checks, the bid arithmetic) take well under a second: they run even when collecting used up
# its time, otherwise the submitter would get no bid at all (it then omits every position).
ALWAYS = (Phase.VERIFY, Phase.COMPUTE, Phase.SUBMIT)
QUICK_BUDGET_S = 30


async def _run_agent(agent: Agent, deadline_bound: bool) -> None:
    try:
        budget = agent.ctx.time_left() if deadline_bound else agent.ctx.seconds_left() - FINAL_MARGIN_S
        if agent.phase in (Phase.VERIFY, Phase.COMPUTE):
            budget = max(budget, QUICK_BUDGET_S)
        await asyncio.wait_for(agent.run(), timeout=max(1.0, budget))
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, "timed out")
        log.warning("%s timed out", agent.name)
    except Exception as error:
        agent.ctx.board.error(agent.name, f"{type(error).__name__}: {error}")
        log.exception("%s failed", agent.name)


def _position_keys(tender: dict) -> dict:
    try:
        from agents.compute_bid import position_keys
        return {str(p.get("position")): position_keys(tender.get("clarifications") or [], str(p.get("position")))["keys"]
                for p in tender.get("positions") or []}
    except Exception as error:  # noqa: BLE001 - a summary must never fail a run
        return {"error": str(error)[:80]}


def board_summary(board: Blackboard) -> dict:
    """A compact view of what the swarm knows (one log line), so a run's log shows it even if early lines are lost."""
    r = board.results
    erp = r.get("erp") or {}
    return {"pages": {k: sum(1 for e in board.evidence if e.kind == f"{k}.page") for k in ("tender", "spec", "erp", "mail")},
            "positions": len((r.get("tender") or {}).get("positions") or []),
            "qa": len((r.get("tender") or {}).get("clarifications") or []),
            "requirements": sorted(r.get("requirements") or {}),
            "materials": {p: (m.get("material"), m.get("reason")) for p, m in (r.get("materials") or {}).items()},
            "erp": {"materials": len(erp.get("materials") or {}), "conditions": len(erp.get("conditions") or []),
                    "stock": sorted(erp.get("stock") or {})},
            "discount": r.get("discount"),
            # which release mails were resolved, and which keys the Q&A gave each position: the two sides that must
            # meet for packaging, commitments, setup pools, project bonus and condition groups
            "mail_topics": {t: sorted(v) if isinstance(v, dict) else v for t, v in (r.get("mail") or {}).items()},
            "position_keys": _position_keys(r.get("tender") or {}),
            "open_gaps": [g.get("id") for g in r.get("gaps") or []],
            "tips": sum(len(v) for v in (r.get("tips") or {}).values()), "errors": len(board.errors)}


async def run_swarm(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool, env=os.environ):
    board = Blackboard()
    preload = env.get("SWARM_BOARD_IN")
    if preload and not scored:                       # never replay data in a scored run
        board = Blackboard.load(Path(preload))
    ctx = Context(task=task, board=board, llm=LLM(), pool=BrowserPool(playwright), scored=scored)
    classes = select(discover(), None if scored else env.get("SWARM_ONLY"))
    from swarm.browser_agent import _MAIN_TABS, _OWNERS, _OPENERS
    from swarm import guard
    _MAIN_TABS.clear()
    _OWNERS.clear()
    _OPENERS.clear()
    guard._DECISIONS.clear()
    guard._PENDING.clear()
    log.info("agents: %s", [c.__name__ for c in classes])
    try:
        await ctx.pool.prepare()
        for phase in Phase:
            agents = [c(ctx) for c in classes if c.phase == phase]
            if not agents:
                continue
            bound = phase != Phase.SUBMIT
            if phase not in ALWAYS and ctx.time_left() <= 0:
                log.warning("skipping phase %s: out of time", phase.name)
                continue
            log.info("phase %s: %s (%.0fs left)", phase.name, [a.name for a in agents], ctx.seconds_left())
            await asyncio.gather(*(_run_agent(a, bound) for a in agents))
            if phase == Phase.COLLECT:
                # Guard classification tasks are collection work too. None may survive into signing.
                pending = list(guard._TASKS)
                for t in pending:
                    t.cancel()
                await asyncio.gather(*pending, return_exceptions=True)
                from agents import analyze_discount, analyze_materials, analyze_quantities, analyze_requirements
                await analyze_quantities.publish(ctx)
                await analyze_requirements.publish(ctx)
                await analyze_discount.publish(ctx)
                await analyze_materials.publish(ctx)
                log.info("board after collect (%.0fs left): %s", ctx.seconds_left(), board_summary(board))
            if not scored:
                board.dump(BOARD_DUMP)
        log.info("model calls: %d tokens: %s errors: %d", ctx.llm.calls, ctx.llm.tokens, len(board.errors))
        if (task.get("submission") or {}).get("kind", "api") != "api":
            receipt = board.get("submission") or {}
            if not receipt.get("accepted"):
                raise RuntimeError("No confirmed portal receipt; the run did not verify submission")
            log.info("portal acceptance confirmed: %s", receipt.get("reference"))
            return None                      # a "site" submission was entered by the submitter agent
        answer = board.get("answer")
        if answer is None:
            raise RuntimeError("No schema-valid API answer was produced")
        return answer

No, run_9dff is not going well. It will score 0.

**What went wrong:**
- **3:53:** the browser connection dropped for both the tender and the mail scraper, and both crashed.
- **7:47 and 8:56:** the coordinator's follow-up searches recovered the tender positions and the 5 % discount.
- **10:04:** the agent froze completely. It wrote no log lines and made no model calls after that. Even the 60 s planning limit never fired, so something blocked the agent's event loop. It never submitted, and at 22+ minutes the platform still shows it as "running".

**The two handoff runs finished; I had misread their clocks earlier:**
- **run_c77f: quality 60.3, the new best (was 59.2), signed.** All 5 positions have the right material, quantity and base price. Points were lost exactly where the mail data was missing: discount entered as 0 (the right value is 5, found by run_b392 and run_9dff), surcharge and packaging empty on every position, so unit prices, total, lead times and the price-index check were wrong too. That's what the mail change targets.
- **run_b392: quality 35.6, signed.** The TAN fix worked and the discount was right, but positions 01.02–01.04 were left out.

**What I did:**
- Commit `84284c7` retries the dropped browser connection, and one failed mail search no longer stops the mail scraper.
- The next commit makes the agent print every thread's stack to the log if its event loop stops for 45 s, so a repeat freeze shows where it hangs.
- I started a new test run, `run_f25724cb21e60d3d`: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/run_f25724cb21e60d3d. It has all three changes. The monitor saves its log and reports milestones and the score here.

Should I cancel run_9dff? It can only score 0, and it may still hold one of the team's 3 test-run slots until the platform ends it.

content.text:
I've made the fix and started test run `run_5bc6fc939fb13036` to check it; it has no score yet. The 35.6 traces mainly to mail data that wasn't found in time, with one gap in the code.

**Why 35.6 instead of 60.3:**
- **01.02–01.04 left out (−39):** these positions give a usable stroke, and the right cylinder depends on the end reserves in the technical-release mail. Without that mail, the matcher treats every candidate as unverified and drops the position. All three runs fit this: c77f had the mail and bid all 5 positions; b392 and f257 didn't and lost exactly these three.
- **No surcharge anywhere, metal-index check 0 (about −11.5):** the price-index mail was missing.
- **No packaging (−6.5):** the packaging mail was missing.
- **Unit prices, total and arithmetic wrong:** these follow from the three gaps above.
- **Why the mails were missing:** all three were still unread when the mail lanes ran out of time at 8:35. FX, which converts the USD base prices, was also missing.

**What I changed** (commit `3fea7d1` on `kurk-s/mail-topics`, pushed; 154 tests pass):
- **Search order by points at stake:** discount, technical release, price index, FX, packaging, condition rules, project bonus, setup pools, delivery commitments. The technical-release search also names the reserve keys the specification refers to.
- **Second try:** a search that stops unfinished goes once more to the end of its lane. In f257 the packaging search had already found the right mail when it ran out of steps.
- **More time:** the mail scraper stops 90 s before the end of collection instead of 150 s, about 60 s more.
- **Fewer wasted steps:** if a results list shows no links, the model now clicks the subject once and reads the message instead of searching the page for links.
- **Matcher fallback:** if the reserve is still unknown and exactly one active candidate fits on everything else and has a stroke above the usable travel, it takes that one and marks it "end reserve unverified". With several such candidates it still makes no guess. Your teammate's test shows why: there, "shortest stroke above" would pick the wrong cylinder.

**Not fixed:** 01.05's lead time. It was wrong in f257 (12 weeks) even with all delivery commitments found. Without the board data I can't tell whether the commitment cap is below 130 pieces or the stock reading is off, so I didn't guess.

The test run's log is now saved complete as it comes in, in `.swarm/runs/run_5bc6fc939fb13036-log.md`; earlier copies kept only the tail. For it to beat run_c77f's 60.3, the board summary at the end of collection needs to list technical release, price indices and packaging, and the bid needs all 5 positions. I'll report as it runs: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/run_5bc6fc939fb13036

Collection in run_5bc6 went much better: the bid now has all 5 positions again. It's signing now and the score isn't in yet. I expect it above run_f257's 35.6 and probably near run_c77f's 60.3.

**What the search-order change fixed in run_5bc6:**
- The technical-release mail was read at 3:53, and all 5 positions got a material, including 01.02–01.04 (worth 39 points).
- Also found: discount 5 %, FX, all 3 condition rules, all 5 delivery commitments, the setup pool. Nothing was left out of the bid.

**Still missing in run_5bc6:** the price-index, packaging and project-bonus mails were read but not used. So surcharge, packaging and bonus are empty, and with them the unit prices and the metal-index check. The price-index mail was correct: exact reference, authorised sender, a rate window that covers the scenario date. The probable causes are in the analyst and the search-done check:

1. **Price index:** an empty newer record, such as a result-list row taken for a message, could override the record that has the rates. Records without rates no longer count.
2. **Packaging and bonus:** the model probably called the search done after saving only the result list. A topic now gets one more try whenever the analyst still has no valid mail for it, even if the model said done. The retry is told to open the messages themselves.
3. **Diagnosis:** at the end of mail collection, the analyst now logs every mail it rejected and why (sender, reference, date, no data). If a fix doesn't hold, the next log shows the exact reason.
4. **Late pages:** the analyst now processes pages saved during its last pass before finishing; those were silently lost before.

Commit `4242e88` (156 tests pass) is in the next test run, **`run_69653d1986f86a10`**: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/runs/run_69653d1986f86a10. I'll report run_5bc6's score as soon as it's in, then follow this run.

content.text:
The mail browser itself went down. This isn't the CPU-load problem I described before.

**What the log shows:**
- **0:29–0:34:** the very first navigation to the mail site got stuck in the mail browser (CDP port 9225, the platform's browser 4), before the ERP was busy.
- **2:34–3:50:** the mail login never got past "Login page loaded"; its page-state captures timed out three times. The ERP had separate state timeouts on its own browser at 3:10–3:41.
- **4:02:** the reconnect logic gave up on the login, and my 3 lanes started.
- **4:11:** each of the 3 lane tabs found the old mail login tab hung and closed it. The browser's debug endpoint on 9225 then stopped answering.
- **4:11–4:25:** my new retry (2 s, 5 s) ran, but the browser stayed gone: "browser 3 does not respond", then "browser 3 is unreachable: continuing in a new tab of browser 0". The "browser 3" in those lines is our 0-based index, so it is the mail browser.
- **4:58:** the mail lanes are logging in again, now inside the tender scraper's browser.

So the mail browser crashed or hung completely. The existing fallback (ksiox1337's code) moved mail to the tender browser, which works but costs time. Mail searching effectively starts at about 5:00 instead of 0:45. In run_5bc6 the mail browser worked fine with the same 3 lanes, so this is either a browser instability on the platform, or the 3 lanes plus the hung login tab tipped it over. One run isn't enough to say which.

**What it means for this run:** only about 3½ minutes of mail time are left before the mail cutoff, so expect fewer mails than in run_5bc6. The fixes in this package (rates only from records that have them, the rejection log, the retry based on coverage) can still show up for whatever it reads.

You stopped my last change, so I'm not editing anything. Three options:
1. Do nothing until this run's score and its "mail not counted" log line are in; then we know whether the analyst fixes work.
2. Reduce the risk of the crash: open fewer mail tabs (2 lanes instead of 3), or make the lanes wait until the main tab's login has succeeded instead of starting when it's abandoned.
3. Leave the mail code alone and investigate the browser crash on its own.

I recommend 1 first. Which do you want?

I found what froze run_9dff and run_69653: a bug in a library browser-use is built on, which I can fix in our code. I haven't changed any code since you stopped my last edit, and I need your OK before I add the patch.

**run_69653: Quality 0.** The stall watchdog caught the freeze. The library is `bubus` 1.5.6, browser-use's event bus. Its main loop reads like this:

```python
while self._is_running:
    try:
        await self.step()      # asserts at once if the bus was torn down
    except Exception:
        log...                 # and loops again
```

When the event bus behind a browser session gets torn down while its loop still runs, `step()` fails immediately without ever pausing. The loop logs the error and tries again forever. Because it never pauses, nothing else in the agent can run: no logs, no model calls, no timeouts. That's exactly what run_9dff showed. In run_69653 the error appears 1,139 times, starting right after the mail browser died. So the freeze comes from a browser dying, through this library bug, and can happen in any run where a browser crashes.

**run_5bc6:** its log stops at 00:36:50 ("No confirmed portal receipt") with no spin, so it will most likely score 0 because signing failed on 01.02. The platform still shows it as running.

**Proposed fix**, a few lines added in `swarm/browser_agent.py` and loaded once at import:
- `EventBus.step` returns at once and marks the bus as stopped if the bus isn't started. That ends the endless loop instead of spinning.
- A unit test that reproduces the spin and checks that the loop now exits.

`swarm/browser_agent.py` belongs to the runtime owners (CRUBSTERINO / ksiox1337), so this should be flagged to them.

**What's open overall:**
1. This freeze, fixed by the patch above.
2. The submitter looping on 01.02 (run_5bc6).
3. Packaging and bonus mails read but not counted. That fix is committed (`4242e88`) but hasn't been tested yet, because run_69653 lost its mail browser.

# OWNER: (name)   ROLE: submitter   NEEDS: results["bid"], results["brief"]   WRITES: enters the bid on the tender portal, signs
"""Enters the computed bid in the tender portal's submission wizard and signs it with the TAN from the webmail.

The model drives the wizard (browser 0) from the brief's submission instructions and a table of the values to enter;
`fill_form` sets many fields per step. When the wizard asks for the signing TAN the model calls `get_signing_tan`,
which runs a short browse on the mail browser (3) to read the newest TAN mail. Runs even if earlier phases failed:
then every position without data is omitted ("partial submission"), the bid is still signed.
"""
import time
from decimal import Decimal
from swarm.normalize import de_number
import asyncio

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

from swarm import Agent, Phase, register
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import ActionResult, browse, read_current_page, BrowserSession
from swarm.context import FINAL_MARGIN_S
from swarm.extract import brief_section
from swarm.sites import site_for


class TanParams(BaseModel):
    new_request: bool = Field(default=False, description="True only after explicitly requesting a replacement TAN in the portal")
    requested_at: str = Field(default="", description="when you requested the TAN (as shown), if known")


class ReceiptParams(BaseModel):
    quote: str = Field(description="Exact text on the current portal page confirming the bid was submitted, not saved as draft")
    reference: str = Field(description="Tender reference for this receipt")


def bid_table(bid: dict, tender: dict) -> str:
    lines = []
    answer = bid.get("answer") or {}
    by_pos = {e["position"]: e for e in answer.get("positions") or []}
    for line in bid.get("lines") or []:
        pos = line["position"]
        if pos not in by_pos:
            lines.append(f"- Position {pos}: OMIT this position (use the omit/skip option for it).")
            continue
        e, disp = by_pos[pos], line.get("display") or {}
        req = {k: v for k, v in (line.get("configuration") or {}).items() if v} or line.get("required") or {}
        extra = ", ".join(f"{label} {disp[k]}" for k, label in (("base_unit_price", "base price per piece before discount"),
                                                                  ("surcharge_per_unit", "surcharges per piece"),
                                                                  ("packaging_per_unit", "packaging per piece"),
                                                                  ("rebate_total", "project bonus for the whole position"))
                          if k in disp)
        lines.append(f"- Position {pos}: configuration bore {req.get('bore')}, stroke {req.get('stroke')}, mounting "
                     f"{req.get('mounting')}, certification {req.get('certification')} -> material {e['material_number']}; "
                     f"quantity {e['quantity']} pieces; net unit price {disp.get('unit_price')} EUR; lead time "
                     f"{e['lead_time_weeks']} weeks; breakdown (optional fields): {extra or 'leave empty'}")
    known = {line["position"] for line in bid.get("lines") or []}
    for p in (tender or {}).get("positions") or []:
        if str(p.get("position")) not in known:
            lines.append(f"- Position {p.get('position')}: OMIT this position.")
    return "\n".join(lines) or "- (no position data: omit every position the form shows)"


@register
class BidSubmitter(Agent):
    phase = Phase.SUBMIT
    browser = 0

    async def run(self) -> None:
        ctx = self.ctx
        if ctx.task.get("submission", {}).get("kind") == "api":
            return
        bid = ctx.board.get("bid") or {"answer": {"decision": "bid", "positions": []}, "lines": []}
        facts = ctx.board.get("brief") or {}
        if bid.get("validation_errors"):
            self.log.warning("Bid validation issues require repair in the wizard: %s", bid["validation_errors"])
        answer = bid["answer"]
        tender_site = await site_for(ctx, "tender")
        mail_site = (ctx.board.get("sites") or {}).get("mail")
        site = ctx.site(tender_site)
        creds = site.get("credentials") or {}
        contact = ctx.board.get("mailbox") or ""
        started = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC", time.gmtime())
        decision = answer.get("decision", "bid")
        goal = (
            f"Site (tender portal): {site['url']}\nLogin: username {creds.get('username')!r}, password {creds.get('password')!r}\n\n"
            f"SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS FROM BRIEF:\n{brief_section(ctx.brief, 'Submission', 'Abgabe') or ctx.brief[-2500:]}\n\n"
            f"YOUR JOB: submit exactly ONE signed bid for tender {answer.get('tender_reference') or facts.get('tender_reference')}.\n"
            f"Bidder company: {facts.get('bidder_company')}; VAT id (USt-IdNr.): {facts.get('bidder_vat_id')}"
            f"{'; contact e-mail: ' + contact if contact else ''}.\n"
            f"Decision: {'main offer (bid)' if decision == 'bid' else 'no bid (declaration of non-participation)'}.\n"
            f"Discount percent: {de_number(Decimal(str(answer.get('discount_percent') or 0)))}. Net total: {bid.get('total_display', '0,00')} EUR "
            f"(enter numbers in German format exactly as given).\n"
            f"POSITIONS (form may ask in different order: always read which position it shows):\n"
            f"{bid_table(bid, ctx.board.get('tender') or {})}\n\n"
            "How to work: log in, accept cookies, open tender, register interest if needed, open bid submission. Close "
            "survey popups with their x button. Each step saves only with its continue/next button; going back clears "
            "later steps -> get each step right before continuing. fill_form sets many fields of a step in one action: "
            "cascading selects -> pass apply_button (button applying the selection); set configuration first, then "
            "material, quantity, prices, lead time; then_click continue button. Unsure -> check step result with "
            "read_page (selects may default to wrong option). Fill actual editable controls only. Read-only outputs and "
            "group labels are not checkboxes. If a form reports invalid format, inspect the entered number format first. "
            "Do not repeatedly search for a nonexistent control. Acknowledge tender documents, tick nothing the brief does "

def _stop_torn_down_bus() -> None:
    """bubus 1.5: EventBus._run_loop calls step() while _is_running and logs + retries every error. Once a session's bus
    is torn down (its queue gone, e.g. after its browser died) step() fails its first assert before awaiting anything,
    so the loop spins without ever yielding and freezes the whole event loop: no log line, no model call, no timeout
    (runs 9dff and 6965: 1139 'must be called before step()' errors, then silence). Such a bus now stops instead."""
    from bubus.service import EventBus
    original = EventBus.step
    if getattr(original, "_stops_torn_down_bus", False):
        return

    async def step(self, *args, **kwargs):
        if not (self._on_idle and self.event_queue):
            self._is_running = False
            await asyncio.sleep(0)
            return None
        return await original(self, *args, **kwargs)

    step._stops_torn_down_bus = True
    EventBus.step = step


_stop_torn_down_bus()

content.text:
You were right to look. I made two mistakes and have fixed both:

1. **The change you rejected ran anyway.** It was still in `agents/scrape_mail.py`, uncommitted, and `atira test-run .` uploads the folder as it is on disk. So run_067a contains it: the extra mail tabs start before the main tab's login. I've reverted the file. The working tree is clean now, all 157 tests pass, and nothing extra is committed or pushed. I noted it in `.swarm/runs/INDEX.md` and saved a memory to check `git status` before every test run.
2. **Wrong commit hash.** Earlier I named the fix commit `9c1e1f4`. The real one is **`76d3325`** (bubus freeze and submitter rule).

**What your log shows:** from 1:03 to 2:30 all four browsers hit state-capture timeouts at the same time — tender, spec, ERP and mail. The sandbox's 4 vCPUs were overloaded during startup. The rejected change made that worse, because 2 extra mail tabs logged in during exactly that window. With the revert, the extra tabs start only after the main mail login again, as in run_5bc6, where startup was fine.

**run_067a is still useful for two things:** whether the bubus fix prevents a freeze, and whether signing survives a position that won't save. Its mail result doesn't count as a test, because the package isn't what's committed. The mail browser recovered at 3:30 (00:56:57) and the lanes are searching. I'll report the end and the score.

Two things in this log explain why the technical release and the price index were missing again:

1. **Retried at the end, too late.** The technical release and the price index were the first searches in their lanes. Both died during the startup overload: one ended after 1 step on browser timeouts, the other after 2 steps with only the login done. My retry rule then put them at the end of their lanes, so they only restarted at 9:11 and 9:14, after collection was effectively over. A search that aborts after 1–2 steps (a browser problem, not a real attempt) should be retried right away, not at the end.
2. **The model knew the link but never opened it.** For example: "The message content is in a locked iframe at /messages/calc-6452. Need to read this URL". Then its step budget ran out. The retry should be given that summary, so it opens the link directly.
